title: The Pale House
premise: Bram Hartwell, a nonbinary teacher haunted by twelve years of rationalized noises, inherits their grandmother's house and discovers the family photographs now show an extra chair that wasn't there before. The chair belongs to something beneath the old well — a presence that fills missing children with song until they walk into the water, and it has marked Bram's most vulnerable student, Wren. To save Wren, Bram must learn the song's final verse from their grandmother's buried letters without ever singing along themselves, because the verse only works when spoken, not sung. In the end, Bram speaks the last verse as the well refills, trading their own voice for Wren's freedom, and finds an unexpected found family in Wren's mother and the school's caretaker, who help them build a new life in the pale house.
about_author: Theo Joubert is the pen name of a former rural schoolteacher who spent a decade collecting local ghost stories from the farming communities where they taught. They write quiet horror about inheritance and the things families refuse to name.

chapters.title: The Extra Chair
chapters.summary: POV: Bram. After their grandmother's funeral, Bram moves into the inherited house and begins teaching at Hollow Creek School, where three students have gone missing over two years. Sorting through old photographs, Bram notices every image of grandma's kitchen now includes an empty wooden chair against the wall. The emotional beat is dread disguised as grief — Bram's lifelong habit of explaining away the inexplicable begins to crack.

chapters.title: The Song Beneath the Well
chapters.summary: POV: Bram, with interludes from Wren's journal. Bram bonds with Wren, a withdrawn student who hums a melody no one taught them — the same tune Bram heard through the floorboards as a child. Investigating the sealed well behind the house, Bram finds grandma's hidden letters describing 'the singing water' and a final verse she never wrote down. The beat: love against duty, as Bram realizes protecting Wren means facing what the family buried.

chapters.title: Refill
chapters.summary: POV: Bram and alternating chapters from Wren. The well begins to refill after years dry; children across town start humming in unison, and Wren sleepwalks toward the water twice. The caretaker, Odile, reveals her own sister was taken decades ago, and together they decode grandma's letters: the last verse exists only in memory, held by whatever waits below. The beat is rising panic — the song is nearly complete, and Wren knows all but one line.

chapters.title: Spoken, Not Sung
chapters.summary: POV: Bram. On the night the well refills, Wren walks into the yard singing, and Bram follows, learning the final verse by listening to the thing in the water — then speaking it aloud instead of joining the melody. The presence recoils; the well collapses inward and goes silent forever, but Bram loses their voice for a season. The resolution: Wren's mother and Odile move into the pale house with Bram, and the photographs finally show only the people who belong there.
